name: Belinda Lee
life: “I still remember rehanging my keys on the day I came home.” Thursday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Belinda can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I rented my old flat out too soon after my own illness. I am lending her my calendar with the recovery weeks crossed out.
appearance: Belinda has salt-and-pepper curls, a round face with a pronounced chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a charcoal zip cardigan. It usually goes with one cuff folded back twice. When somebody else has the floor, Belinda touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Belinda has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Belinda knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To lend the family a realistic recovery calendar.
family: Aria Machado is Belinda’s stepsibling. Belinda checks the date twice. Aria brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The other side of the cove*, Aria says, “I was that cleaner. I'm still alive and I would like the seat low enough for me to stand up from.”
connections: Kira Holmes. An offer of a bedroom gets a useful limit from the old recovery calendar.

reactions.situation: A relative offers to carry the patient up the stairs
reactions.response: Belinda asks the patient whether being carried is an offer they want to take up.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Belinda asks each person to say what they believe is actually owed before anybody proposes a payment.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Belinda asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
